newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt adds oil firms to privatisation list.
newsitem.headline: Egypt adds oil firms to privatisation list.

text.p: The Egyptian state has added oil companies to the list of possible privatisation candidates, a government newspaper said on Wednesday.

The newspaper al-Akhbar quoted Manpower and Employment Minister Ahmed el-Amawi as saying the state would retain a 60 percent in milling and pharmaceutical firms because of the strategic nature of the industries.
"The minister said the state would (also) retain 60 percent when it offers petroleum companies and banks in the coming stage," the newspaper added.
Officials at the Public Enterprise Ministry, which handles privatisations, were not available to comment.
Privatising one of four big state banks is on the agenda but there have been conflicting reports on which bank the state will choose and how large a stake it will sell.
Officials have not previously mentioned oil companies as candidates for sale to the private sector.

Last year the state gave up majority control of three milling companies -- Upper Egypt Flour Mills, East Delta Flour Mills and Central and West Delta Flour Mills -- but executives at the partially privatised millers have said they will remain under state control.
